questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to go to Italy first of all. I have lived there many years and have a strong connection to the country and I wanted to go back.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy! We were will informed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Just the e-mails from Mobilityonline which were super helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Check Spotahome! I ended up finding a private host through a Facebook group.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive but you have a lot more freedom. Some on-campus facilities will not allow you to have guests etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty confusing, a lot of deadlines and some miscommunications between the institutions which turned out to solve itself but it stressed me out a lot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Massimo was available on e-mail but sometimes takes a bit to reply

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy since I have open electives. Only struggles was the time tables of different classes clashing sometimes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Think about the exam when you register. Oral exams in Italy are in front of the whole class, written exams are by hand and usually graded quite hard. So maybe my advice would be to not be too over-confident when choosing subjets, you will have more fun if you choose something managable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of learning by memory and uninspiring teachers. Everything was very old-school and it was very had to figure out what was expected of us.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is generally quite 'low' compared to Denmark, but the exams questions and the way they percieve knowledge consumption is so different from ours in Denmark. Expect direct questions to small bits of the curriculum, no analysis or broad questions.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I replied to that above. Way more old-school and not as collaborative. Hours of talking and no breaks.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Globalization, Social Justice and Human Rights 
Geopolitics of Migrations 
Mythology and its Media
British Theatre History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: British Theatre History was interesting and well-structured. The exam was oral and a bit scary but the teacher was good at preparing us.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs really but I was suprised by how expensive Milan was. It was very overwhelming.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was insane. But also general shopping and groceries can become very expensive if you're not good at budgeting. The metro card was super cheap and easy!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many Erasmus events but also academic clubs and sport facilites

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you are looking for friends in the beginning, go to the Erasmus parties etc. 
Also eat in the cafeteria at the campus and talk to people in the classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Milan gives you a great starting point to travel Italy! I went to Bergamo, Crema, Como, Firenze, Rome and Genova.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have lived in Italy many years and speak Italian so for me it was like returning home. But Italy can be overwhelming if you are not accustomed to it, but that is part of the beauty of exchange to discover a new culture without too many inputs to influence you before.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found Milanese people to be quite cold compared to the south where I have lived before. Also Milan is big and transportation (though organised) takes a long time. Especially during the night when the metro closes, it is impossible to get around which was also expensive because then you have to take a taxi.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love Italy. So everything. Language, the people, the music, the bars, the coffee shop, the food. Go to Italy if you wanna emerge in this, otherwise it will probably be stressful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Save up a lot of money. 
2. Stay in a place that is well connected with metro or tram. Busses can be a bit unreliable. 
3. Remember how lucky you are to have the opportunity to go on exhange! So enjoy it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask for help and even though uni is very different and sometime stressful, remember to go enjoy Italy during the time off. Travel!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know Milan and meeting some of my new best friends. Socially it was way over my expectations and I had so much fun.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably money. It was very expensive. Also some areas are not extremely safe so be careful around certain zones especially at night.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
